questions.text:
Okay. She's out running and her phone's sitting on our counter. 🙃
For a month some guy's been dropping her off around 2 a.m. in a grey car, engine running till she's inside.
Five years living together and she's never hidden a guy from me.
Who's the guy driving her home at 2 a.m.?

Nate. Doesn't ring a single bell.
Last night she rolled in at 2 again, told me she was out with work people. Nobody from a pharmacy is out at 2 a.m.
Where exactly did she and Nate meet up last night?

Dana? She's the kid who covers Bea's shifts when she's sick. Sweet as anything.
So it's a work thing. Bea, Dana, and some stranger with a grey car.
What does Nate actually do for a living?
questions.hint: Check Mail for a message from him.

A reporter. Not a boyfriend, not a dealer. A reporter. 😳
All I know about reporters is from movies. They never use real names for the people who talk to them.
What name does Nate call her by?

I've wrapped fish in that paper. Now it's got my roommate in it.
She's not dating a reporter. She's feeding him a story, and I'd bet it's about somebody at work.

Opioids. From the counter she stands behind every day. 💔
The other day she texted me she was off on a long run by the river. Came home bone dry.
Where exactly was she during that long run by the river?

onboarding.text: It's 7 a.m. Bea's out running, and for the first time in a month she left her phone behind. It's sitting on our counter, buzzing. I'm Owen. I cook for a living, and I'm terrible at waiting.
onboarding.label: Owen

onboarding.text: Five years ago she answered my roommate ad, showed up with burnt enchiladas, and lectured me about my sleep schedule. We've split every rent check, every breakup and every bad night since then. She's family.
onboarding.label: Owen & Beatriz

onboarding.text: Bea Castellano. Pharmacist at Corlew, tortoiseshell glasses, runs ten miles for fun. Lately a stranger drops her off at 2 a.m., she makes me keep the curtains shut, and she flinches whenever her phone lights up.
onboarding.label: Beatriz

onboarding.text: Maybe she's in over her head with some guy. Maybe somebody's scaring her. She won't tell me. So help me go through her phone one question at a time, before she gets back.
onboarding.label: Owen

gmail.body:
Owen,

I've started this letter four times. You'll know why when you read the next part, and I need you to hear it from me and not from somebody else.

I kept all of it from you so you wouldn't have to testify. Ingrid says nobody can make you repeat what you never knew. If Carl's lawyers ever ask, you really don't know anything. That's the point. They can't subpoena what's not in your head.

I hated every night I lied to your face. I'm sorry for the curtains and for the headlights. You're the best person I know, and you make the worst short rib in the world, by which I mean the best, and I'm going to miss it so much.

Don't wait up for me. When this is over I'll tell you everything over a plate of whatever you're making.

Bea
